expected_effect: Completed steps at 1800 s rise by +8% to +20% (2237-2490 on trn21-equivalent hosts) because the 537M-parameter table gather/scatter/RMSprop/clip work is removed. Predeclared BPB direction: public_val_bpb lower than the same-host control by 0.002-0.008 (from ~1.0057 to ~0.998-1.004). If BPB is not lower despite >=8% more steps, the hypothesis is falsified (tables are worth their step cost at this budget); if the step gain is below 8%, the throughput mechanism is falsified.
hypothesis: At the pinned 9a4caa7b default shape the model is 592.9M parameters, of which the hashed n-gram value-embedding tables alone are 4 tables x 1,048,576 rows x 128 dim = 536.9M (control ledger oneliner 'ngram_ve: True tables=4 rows=1048576 dim=128 ... opt=rmsprop bf16=True'), leaving roughly 56M dense transformer parameters. Two smoke rows at this commit show that per-step maintenance of that table block is a first-order throughput cost: --ngram-rms-fp32 (only the table RMSprop state math changed) dropped steps from 335 to 316 (-5.7%), and --weight-ema (one extra elementwise pass over all parameters, dominated by the tables) dropped steps from 334 to 313 (-6.3%). Removing the tables entirely (gather, backward scatter, RMSprop update, clip-norm contribution, index computation) should therefore raise the completed step count at the fixed 1800 s budget by at least 8%. Hypothesis: within a 30-minute budget the n-gram tables cost more in lost dense-model optimizer steps than they return in quality, so the dense-only model at seed 42 reaches a lower public_val_bpb than the same-host control. Supporting but confounded prior: the entire fresh-start lineage and the frozen candidate submissions/dense6x1024_public0992851/train.py run with --no-ngram-ve and score 0.979-0.993 public (fs-w65, fs-w98, fs-w146, CURRENT_STATE.md) versus 1.0057 for the ngram-enabled default; those runs differ in depth/width/eval settings, so they motivate but do not establish the isolated effect this run measures.
single_causal_change: Pass --no-ngram-ve only. Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls: identical launch shape (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000, --max-train-seconds 1800, --seed 42), identical environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1), no precision flag, no kernel/compile flag, no optimizer-rule, schedule, batch, evaluation, or other architecture change. No other --ngram-ve-* option is passed. The only behavioral delta is that the hashed n-gram value-embedding tables and their RMSprop optimizer are not constructed or trained; the dense transformer, its optimizer, data order, and evaluator are unchanged. Pre-full inertness check: the candidate's resolved 'ngram_ve' oneliner must read 'False tables=0' and num_params_M must fall from 592.9 to roughly 56 (>=500M fewer); if either does not hold, classify FALSIFIED-INERT without spending the full run. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb at the fixed 1800 s budget (trn21 -> 2071 steps / 1.005734; trn22 -> 2076 steps / 1.005967). Because the hypothesis is explicitly a fixed-budget tradeoff (fewer parameters, more steps), the primary comparison is the fixed-budget public_val_bpb; no matched-step equivalence is claimed. Outcome classes, mutually exclusive, evaluated in order: (1) FALSIFIED-INERT per the pre-full check above; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if candidate steps < 90% of same-host control steps (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22; experiment-protocol.md section 5 rule; record as throughput regression only); (3) FALSIFIED-THROUGHPUT if steps < +8% of control (<2237 trn21, <2242 trn22): the table-cost mechanism is falsified regardless of BPB; record BPB for information only; (4) SUCCESS if steps >= +8% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by at least 0.002; (5) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +8% and public_val_bpb >= same-host control (the tables return more quality than their step cost at this budget); (6) INCONCLUSIVE if steps >= +8% and the BPB improvement is between 0 and 0.002 (within the 0.00023 inter-host control spread plus margin).
